source.title: Leveraging Passage Retrieval with Generative Models for Open Domain Question Answering

claims.summary: Closed-book generative QA must store factual information in model weights and therefore relies on very large models that are expensive to train and query.
FiD follows a two-step approach: retrieve support passages from an external knowledge source, then generate an answer conditioned on the question and passages.

locator.label: Figure 1
locator.selection: Question, retrieved support passages, generative seq2seq model, and answer flow

claims.summary: FiD encodes each question-passage pair independently, concatenates the resulting representations, and lets one decoder attend jointly over them to generate the answer.

locator.label: Figure 2
locator.selection: Independent encoders, representation concatenation, shared decoder, and answer

claims.summary: Independent passage encoding keeps encoder self-attention local to one context, so computation grows linearly rather than quadratically with the number of passages.
Joint decoder attention over concatenated passage representations is intended to aggregate evidence across multiple passages.
The paper uses either BM25 or DPR for support-passage retrieval; FiD itself contributes the generative reader rather than a new retriever.
The generative reader can be initialized from T5 or BART and formats each input from the question, passage title, and passage text.
The experiments use DPR retrieval for Natural Questions and TriviaQA and BM25 retrieval for SQuAD, so dataset results do not share one retriever setting.
Answers are evaluated with normalized Exact Match: a generated answer is correct if it matches an acceptable reference after normalization.
On the Natural Questions test setting, FiD-large reports 51.4 Exact Match, FiD-base 48.2, RAG 44.5, and DPR 41.5.

claims.summary: The retriever is not trained jointly with FiD in this work; integrating retrieval and learning the complete system end-to-end are listed as future work.
The empirical scope is open-domain question answering on Natural Questions, TriviaQA, and SQuAD Open rather than general-purpose generation tasks.
The experiments retrieve fixed-length, non-overlapping Wikipedia passages, making the passage the unit processed independently by the encoder.
The authors interpret the improvement with more retrieved passages as evidence that seq2seq models can combine information from multiple passages.
claims.section: 4 Experiments - Scaling with number of passages

claims.summary: The conclusion identifies efficiency at large passage counts as an open problem alongside joint retriever integration.
